messages:
carla: FYI saw a latency regression on AWQ INT8 inference on the t4 pool after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. p95 is up ~18% for our short-chat workload. profiling below.

carla: ```
pprof summary (short-chat, batch=1, seq<=64):
- pack_time_total: 3120ms (2.6ms/request, prev ~480ms total)
- pack_cache_hits: 12 / 1200
- matmul:int8_fast: 0.9ms
- matmul:generic_int8: 3.4ms
- kv_cache_miss_penalty: +1.2ms avg
callers: runtime/pack.go:142, runtime/selector.go:78
```

ben: did the selector start falling back to generic_int8 for small shapes? that's usually the culprit. which model/config?

carla: gpt-3-small-awq, AWQ weight-only, group_size=128, pack format AWQ32. selector logs show chosen kernel: generic_int8 when seq_len<=64 && batch==1. new heuristic prefers single-threaded code-path for tiny batches.

dan: suspect we're repacking weights on the hot path. if packing isn't cached per model variant we pay that ~2.4ms every request. can you `--dump-packing-stats`?

carla: ```
# runtime --dump-packing-stats
pack_calls: 1200
pack_cache_hits: 12
avg_pack_latency_ms: 2.6
persisted_packed_weights: false
```

emily: oof. repacking on every request = guaranteed p95 inflation. we should persist packed weights on model load; why didn't we?

ben: the selector change introduced a per-request flag `repack_for_batch` to support dynamic group remapping. looks like it was set true for group_size>64 by mistake, causing a repack for AWQ formats.

carla: confirmed. quick experiment: force reuse_packed=true by env and rerun.

carla: ```
before (default): p50=22ms p95=76ms
after (REDWOOD_REUSE_PACKED=1): p50=20ms p95=63ms
```

fahad: still a gap vs fp16 baseline though. is the int8_fast kernel underperforming on small matmuls? calibration steps might be adding overhead too.\
dan: two things to consider: 1) group_size=128 gives larger groups -> fewer quant buckets but more per-group unpack compute; try group_size=64. 2) our int8_fast kernel is optimized for big GEMMs; for tiny heads (<64) it can be slower than a compact fp16 path. we need to route small-shapes differently.

carla: microbench results: int8_fast is ~25% faster on big mats (batch*seq*heads large) but 20-40% slower for tiny matmuls (<64x64). our batching heuristic creates many tiny matmuls for short-chat workloads.

ben: proposal: runtime heuristic - if seq_len<=32 && batch<=2 then prefer fp16 kernel to avoid pack/unpack overhead and poor small-matmul int8 perf. we'll A/B on a canary.

emily: also KV cache interplay: when KV cache is hot we avoid the big matmul, but repack triggers when quant params change. include quant-table checksum in packed-format metadata so reuse works across calibration runs that keep the same table.

carla: opened PR to persist packed weights and include checksum + to update selector: https://stash.redwood/REPO/pull/1234 (draft).

perf-bot: nightly-run: awq-int8 canary with REDWOOD_REUSE_PACKED=1 -> p95 -8% vs baseline, throughput stable.

dan: action items:
1) set reuse_packed default=true for dedicated pools (dan)
2) add small-shape -> fp16 heuristic and unit tests for kernel decision matrix (ben)
3) expose packing_ttl and pack_cache_hit metrics in console (dan)
4) include quant-table checksum in packed-format metadata and allow reuse across calibrations (carla)

ben: taking item #2, will add tests and a microbench harness for tiny GEMMs.

carla: thanks all. I'll monitor the canary tomorrow and watch the rollouts dashboard. cc @oncall-ml :thumbsup:
